limits: THE RESUME HALF of the subsumption machinery (issue #1166), and the only control here whose cases span TWO runner invocations. The defect is unreachable in one: a run must defer gates into an aggregate, fail AT the aggregate, and then be resumed. So each case carries its own two-phase driver in `bin/uv` - phase 1 runs the real lib.cicd against `Makefile` and must fail, the driver swaps in `Makefile.phase2`, and phase 2 is the RESUME whose result the gate judges. Phase 1's output goes to stderr so it cannot be read as the verdict. GOOD_EXIT IS 3, NOT 0, AND THAT IS THE HONEST VALUE. A resumed run here carries `security_scan` (it succeeded in phase 1 and does not re-run) across a tree that changed between the phases, and the case tree is not a git repository, so `tree_verified` can never be true and the correct verdict is `warn (carried, unverified: security_scan)`. This control therefore discriminates `warn` - correct - from `fail`, which is what the defect produces; it says nothing about `ok`. Forcing an `ok` would have meant removing the one successful step that sits between the deferred gates and the aggregate, and that step is precisely what makes the defect reachable: without it `current_index` never advances past the deferred gates, the resume re-enters them by accident, and the case would pass on the UNFIXED code. Measured - an earlier draft did exactly that. WHAT THE CASES ESTABLISH. `good-fail-fix-resume`: the tree is fixed, the resumed derivation still subsumes all three, and the retry settles them `subsumed` instead of leaving them `not-run`; on 9162b8e the same input reports `fail (recorded not-run: lint test typecheck)` - a genuinely green retry rejected, naming gates that ran. `bad-makefile-changed-between-runs`: the tree LEAVES lint behind between the runs and lint is still broken, so nothing runs it and the gate must red by REPLAYING it. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT REGISTERED, and why the absence is stated rather than left to silence: the retry-fails-again case. It is covered by `tests/test_runner.py::TestResumeSettlesDeferredGates` and is NOT a case here because it does not discriminate - the correct gate and every candidate anchor both fail it, since an aggregate that fails again leaves the not-run records standing whichever way they were reached. Registering it would score the anchor INERT for a case that was never a test of the anchor. THE ANCHOR IS CONSTRUCTED because no released gate carries this defect: resume-side settlement did not exist before #1166, so no historical article can be blind to it. What it reproduces is the fix #1166's own body prefers and the wave overruled - settle every NOT_RUN record from the PERSISTED map, without asking whether THIS tree's aggregate still runs them.
